title: IAF Helicopter in PM Modi's Convoy Grounded in Mysuru After Technical Snag
excerpt: One of three helicopters in the Prime Minister's convoy could not take off from the Jayachamaraja Wadiyar helipad after his Mysuru programme. Modi continued in another aircraft; technicians are repairing the grounded helicopter.
body:
• An Indian Air Force helicopter in Prime Minister Narendra Modi's convoy developed a technical snag in Mysuru and remained grounded at the Jayachamaraja Wadiyar helipad near Lalit Mahal Palace on Saturday.
  • Three helicopters had arrived for the visit. When the convoy prepared to leave after the Prime Minister's programme, one could not take off.
  • Modi and the rest of the convoy continued their onward journey in one of the other two helicopters. No one was harmed.
  • Technical personnel are repairing the aircraft at the helipad, where police have set up a security cordon. No official statement had specified the nature of the fault or a repair timeline as of Saturday.

An Indian Air Force helicopter assigned to Prime Minister Narendra Modi's convoy remained parked at a Mysuru helipad on Saturday after a technical problem prevented it from taking off with the rest of the fleet, IANS reported.

Modi had arrived in Mysuru at around 3:20 p.m. on Friday for the inauguration of the COSMOS-Mysuru Planetarium. Three helicopters arrived as part of the Prime Minister's convoy and landed at the Jayachamaraja Wadiyar helipad near Lalit Mahal Palace. When the convoy prepared to depart after the programme, one of the aircraft developed a technical problem and could not take off.

The Prime Minister's journey continued

Modi and other members of the convoy continued their onward journey in one of the other two helicopters, Mirror Now reported. The grounded aircraft stayed at the helipad, where local police established a security cordon around it.

Technical personnel have reached the site and are carrying out repair work to make the aircraft fit for further operations. It remained at the helipad at the time of the reports on Saturday.

The visit around the incident

The Mysuru stop was one leg of a Karnataka visit built around inaugurations. Modi arrived in the city on Friday afternoon for the COSMOS-Mysuru Planetarium inauguration, and the same visit included development programmes in Bengaluru. The convoy's helicopters were the transport between those engagements, which is why three aircraft were on the ground at the Jayachamaraja Wadiyar helipad when the fault was found.

What has not been said

No official statement had been issued on the exact nature of the technical snag or on when the helicopter would resume its journey. The incident occurred during the Prime Minister's Karnataka visit, which included development-related programmes in Bengaluru and Mysuru.

VVIP air movements in India operate with multiple aircraft precisely so that a single aircraft fault does not change the principal's schedule — which is what happened here. The open item is narrow: the cause of the fault, and the IAF's timeline for returning the helicopter to service.
